Test Description: Verifies default power-up values and masked write/read compliance across the GPIO per-pin control, group IO control, group data, and interrupt registers.
Remarks: When reading default values without forcing inputs, the input bit may appear high; forcing low at the pad can affect bit-level selection and cause a mismatch with the documented default.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Start the test logic.
2) For each register in the configured list that is not marked as reset-skip and is readable, read the register value and ignore the least significant bit in the comparison.
3) Compare the masked read value against the documented default value and record a default-value error on any mismatch.
4) For each of six predefined test patterns, write the pattern to each register that is marked writable and not in the write-skip set using the documented write-allowed mask.
5) For each register written that is also readable, read back the register value and apply the documented read mask.
6) Compute the expected read-back value by combining the written bits allowed by the write mask with the default values of the bits that are not writable, then apply the read mask.
7) Compare the masked read-back value against the expected value and record a write/read error on any mismatch.
8) After all iterations complete, report pass if no default-value or write/read mismatches were recorded; otherwise report fail.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
Pass if:
1) Every readable, non-reset-skipped register equals its documented default when compared with the least significant bit ignored; and
2) For each writable and readable register, the read-back value after masked write equals the expected value derived from the write permissions and documented defaults; otherwise fail.

Feature: interrupts can be generated based on positive edge or negative edge or level high or level low detection at GPIO input
Test Description: Configures GPIOs 8–39 as inputs with negative-edge detection, enables the group interrupt output, generates one falling edge per pin via the pad driver, services the interrupt, and clears per-pin and group status while verifying input and masked-group status behavior.
Remarks: Bounded timeouts are used and may require adjustment to the simulation time base.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Enable the platform interrupt for the selected GPIO instance.
2) Enable the system interrupt output for the selected GPIO instance by setting the appropriate bit in INTR_EN1.
3) Drive all GPIO pads high via the pad-control address to establish a known idle level.
4) For each pin from GPIO 8 through GPIO 39, program its per-pin control register to input mode, enable negative-edge detection, and clear any pending per-pin raw status; insert a short delay after each write.
5) For the current pin, clear the corresponding bit in GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1 and enable only that bit in INTR1_INTR_EN1; wait briefly.
6) Arm the interrupt-wait flag before generating the edge.
7) Create a falling edge for the current pin by first driving all pads high, then driving only the target pin low with a short delay between transitions.
8) Poll the interrupt-wait flag with a bounded timeout, inserting a fixed delay between polls; if the timeout expires, record an error.
9) In the interrupt handler, deassert the wait flag and return pads to the idle high level.
10) Read the current pin’s per-pin control/status register and confirm its input bit reads low after the falling edge.
11) Read INTR1_INTR_STS1 and confirm only the bit for the current pin is set.
12) Clear the per-pin raw status in the per-pin control register and clear the corresponding bit in GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1.
13) Re-read INTR1_INTR_STS1 and confirm it reads zero.
14) Clear the system raw status for the selected GPIO instance using RAW_STCR1 and clear the platform interrupt.
15) After all pins are tested, report the cumulative result.

Feature: interrupts can be generated based on positive edge or negative edge or level high or level low detection at GPIO input
Test Description: Enables positive-edge detection for GPIOs 8–39, sets them to input mode via group IO control, enables group interrupts, generates one rising edge per pin, services the interrupt, clears per-pin status for all pins and verifies that the group masked-interrupt status is asserted then cleared and that the system raw status is cleared.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Enable the platform interrupt for the selected GPIO instance.
2) Enable the system interrupt output for the selected GPIO instance by setting the appropriate bit in INTR_EN1.
3) For each pin from GPIO 8 through GPIO 39, enable positive-edge detection in its per-pin control register.
4) Configure input mode for GPIOs 8–39 using GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1 through GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP4.
5) Enable all group interrupt bits in INTR1_INTR_EN1.
6) For each pin, ensure pads are low, arm the interrupt-wait flag, then drive pads high to create a single rising edge.
7) Poll the interrupt-wait flag with a bounded timeout, inserting a fixed delay between polls; on timeout, record an error and stop testing further pins.
8) Optionally return pads low and wait briefly to prepare for the next iteration.
9) In the interrupt handler, clear the wait flag and mask group interrupts by writing zero to INTR1_INTR_EN1 during service.
10) Read INTR1_INTR_STS1 and confirm that at least one bit is set, indicating an interrupt occurred.
11) Clear per-pin raw status for all 32 pins by writing the clear field in each per-pin control register.
12) Re-read INTR1_INTR_STS1 and confirm it reads zero.
13) Clear the system raw status for the selected GPIO instance via RAW_STCR1 and verify it is cleared.
14) Re-enable group interrupts in INTR1_INTR_EN1 and clear the platform interrupt before returning to the main loop.
15) Report the cumulative result at test completion.
